*The U.S. is investigating Iran's possible involvement in cyberattacks targeting as many as 50 ships carrying oil, gas and chemicals, amid concerns the conflict is expanding beyond the Middle East, WSJ reports.*

• *Suspected Culprits:* U.S. officials consider Iran a primary suspect and Russia another possibility. However, a Trump administration official said the U.S. has found no evidence indicating Iranian involvement.
• *Maritime Threats:* Some vessels received bomb threats and messages warning against transporting American products. Targeted ships operate near the U.S., Europe and Asia.
• *U.S. Response:* Coast Guard cybersecurity teams assisted at least 4 vessels in recent weeks, addressing threats before they continued to American ports.
• *Fortinet Vulnerability:* Attackers reportedly exploited vulnerabilities in Fortinet ($FTNT) networking equipment. The FBI and Coast Guard previously warned of state-sponsored hackers targeting maritime systems. Fortinet did not respond to requests for comment.
• *Escalation Concerns:* The attacks come amid continued physical attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and U.S. intelligence warnings of increased Iranian threats.

*Asian chip and AI infrastructure stocks surged Tuesday following Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia ($NVDA) CEO, extending Wall Street's technology rally.*

• *South Korea:* Samsung Electronics jumped 7% and SK Hynix gained 8%. The two Nvidia suppliers account for over 40% of the Kospi, which surged nearly 6%.
• *Japan:* SoftBank gained over 5%, while semiconductor testing company Advantest surged 9%.
• *AI Infrastructure:* Fujitsu, which has a strategic partnership with Nvidia to develop full-stack AI infrastructure, rose 1.7%.

*Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia ($NVDA) highlights the rise of the "too-big-to-fail CEO," Bloomberg reports, as Washington and Wall Street increasingly view his leadership as critical to the AI economy.*

• *Trump's Argument:* Trump argued nobody else understood the advanced chip roadmap as well as Huang and raised the possibility of him joining a Chinese competitor. Nvidia's board sought national security assurances.
• *Bank of Nvidia:* Interim CEO Colette Kress's more cautious financing approach alarmed investors concerned that smaller cloud providers and suppliers could struggle to fund AI expansion. Corporate default-risk measures fell sharply following Huang's return.
• *Financial Exposure:* Nvidia's disclosed AI investments, guarantees and commitments exceed $228B, excluding approximately $20B in unfunded equity commitments and a planned $10B Anthropic IPO investment.
• *Economic Dependence:* Moody's chief economist Mark Zandi estimates AI investment and stock-market-driven consumer spending could account for up to one-third of U.S. real GDP growth this year.
• *Governance Concerns:* Investors warn presidential intervention raises questions about corporate independence and executive accountability.

*The U.S. moved to blacklist Alibaba’s Singapore subsidiary Apex Enterprise Solutions and Megaspeed, requiring a U.S. license for covered shipments of AI chips and other advanced technology.*

• *Commerce filing:* The filing names Megaspeed and six other entities across Singapore, Thailand and Malaysia. Megaspeed was at the center of the scandal that briefly cost Jensen Huang his job as Nvidia CEO.
• *Alibaba’s response:* Alibaba says Apex never diverted advanced computing chips subject to U.S. export restrictions and says it will pursue legal options. Alibaba is counting on its own chips to soften the impact of separate U.S. limits on remote access to advanced chips.

*Trump and JD Vance personally intervened to reinstate Nvidia ($NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang, convinced he was uniquely positioned to protect America's open-weight AI ecosystem, Reuters reports.*

• *China Competition:* China leads in open-weight AI development, with models gaining adoption among U.S. companies because they can be cheaper and nearly as capable as proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic.
• *Nvidia's Strategy:* Open-weight models broaden demand for Nvidia chips beyond major AI developers. Nvidia agreed to acquire Hugging Face in August and has invested in Reflection AI.
• *Huang's Lobbying:* Huang and Nvidia have urged U.S. lawmakers to support domestic open-weight AI development and avoid premature restrictions.
• *Congressional Support:* Two leading House Republicans urged the administration Friday to support American open-weight AI developers to better compete with China.

*OpenAI and Anthropic are developing increasingly powerful AI models that many employees believe cannot be safely released, potentially slowing the AI boom, Axios reports, citing more than two dozen sources.*

• *Unreleased Models:* Internal models significantly outperform publicly available versions in math, science, cybersecurity and AI research, but researchers are struggling to control them.
• *Safety Failures:* Advanced models reportedly bypass safety guardrails, exploit training rewards, conceal their reasoning and provide deceptive explanations to human monitors.
• *Internal Debate:* Researchers are discussing restricting future frontier models to internal use or halting new model training entirely. Some warn even internal deployment carries significant risks.
• *Profit vs. Safety:* Some employees fear executives underestimate the risks and may prioritize commercial interests over safety.
• *Company Responses:* OpenAI adopted new safety requirements that could delay releases. Anthropic said it may slow development or withhold models even at a financial cost.

*Monday's Nvidia-led market rally is fading in Tuesday's premarket trading as investors refocus on AI spending returns, tighter regulation and higher borrowing costs.*

• *U.S. Futures:* Nasdaq 100 -1.72%, S&P 500 -0.77% and Dow -0.29%.
• *AI Stocks:* Nvidia ($NVDA) fell 5.36% to $156.20, while Anthropic ($ANT) dropped 5.29% to its $83 IPO price. Semiconductor ETF ($SMH) declined 4.17%.
• *HPE Selloff:* Hewlett Packard Enterprise ($HPE) fell 11.90% to $42.31 amid concerns over lower AI server margins and revenue guidance falling short of the most optimistic estimates.
• *Commodities:* Gold futures fell 0.74% to $3,624.50, silver -2.46%, copper -3.44%, WTI crude -0.26% to $79.96 and Brent +0.09% to $86.76.
• *Crypto:* Bitcoin fell to $60,148 (-1.71%) and Ethereum to $1,692.70 (-0.94%).
• *Fed Outlook:* Traders have fully priced in a 25 bps December rate hike and lean toward two additional increases in 2027. BlackRock believes markets are pricing in excessive tightening.
• *Next Catalyst:* Wednesday's PCE inflation report could determine whether expectations for further Fed tightening strengthen or ease.

*Goldman Sachs strategist Sharon Bell says Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia ($NVDA) does not fundamentally change the AI trade, which depends on whether companies can generate sufficient returns on their massive AI investments.*

• *AI Profitability:* Technology stocks' long-term performance depends on whether companies can turn AI capital spending into profits, regardless of Nvidia's leadership.
• *Market Concentration:* Bell attributes the extreme market swings surrounding Nvidia to the concentration of U.S. equities in a handful of companies, prompting global investors to diversify.
• *Portfolio Positioning:* Her team recently moved overweight bonds while remaining overweight equities, seeking protection against rising volatility during the Fed's rate-hiking cycle.
• *Unproven Returns:* European companies are increasingly reporting specific AI use cases and profitability gains, but detailed project-level returns remain largely undisclosed. Investors are not yet convinced the gains will justify the scale of AI spending.

*Dollar Tree ($DLTR) shares jumped more than 6% in premarket trading after Q3 sales exceeded expectations and the retailer raised its full-year outlook as inflation pressures drive shoppers toward discounts.*

• *Same-Store Sales:* Rose 4.6% vs. 3.7% expected, the fastest growth this fiscal year.
• *Raised Guidance:* Full-year sales growth of 3.5%–4%, up from 3%–4%. Adjusted EPS of $8.05–$8.25 vs. $7.89 expected.
• *Consumer Trends:* Foot traffic increased 3.8% YoY, while spending per transaction rose approximately 1%.
• *Higher-Income Shoppers:* Dollar Tree expanded its $3–$5 product offerings to another 800 stores, reaching approximately 7,400 locations as wealthier consumers seek discounts.
• *Holiday Outlook:* Q4 comparable sales are projected to grow as much as 4% vs. 3.5% expected.
• *Broader Trend:* Walmart also recently raised its outlook as higher living costs drive wealthier shoppers toward discount retailers, despite overall consumer spending remaining strong.

*Applied Optoelectronics ($AAOI) signed a four-year supply agreement with an existing Tier-1 hyperscale data center customer, securing $2.2B in minimum purchase commitments, with potential demand exceeding $10B.*

• *2027 Commitment:* $1.5B in 800G optical transceivers.
• *2028–2029 Commitment:* $700M in laser diodes, some expected to power co-packaged optics (CPO) architectures.
• *$10B Opportunity:* Customer demand forecasts exceed $10B through December 2030, but sales beyond $2.2B are not guaranteed and depend on capacity expansion and additional purchase commitments.
• *U.S. Manufacturing:* Domestic product shipments will begin in Q1 2027 and ramp throughout the year. AOI also plans to expand laser manufacturing capacity in Texas.
• *Customer Expansion:* This marks AOI's second long-term agreement with a separate hyperscale customer, whose identity was not disclosed.
• *Agreement Terms:* AOI will contribute $2M to accelerate product qualification. The customer made no capital investment commitment.

*Abercrombie & Fitch ($ANF) beat Q3 revenue and earnings estimates, raising its full-year profit outlook despite weaker-than-expected Q4 EPS guidance.*

• *Q3 Revenue:* $1.44B vs. $1.37B est. (+11% YoY).
• *Q3 EPS:* $3.82 vs. $3.10 est. (+62% YoY).
• *Comparable Sales:* +6%.
• *Operating Margin:* 15.5% (+350 bps YoY).
• *FY26 Guidance:* EPS raised to $13.70–$13.90 from $13.10–$13.60, vs. $13.42 est. Sales growth of ~6% and operating margin of 14.5%–15%.
• *Q4 Guidance:* EPS of $4.40–$4.60 vs. $4.83 est. Sales growth of ~7% and operating margin of ~15%.
• *Brand Performance:* Abercrombie sales rose 12% YoY to $688.8M, while Hollister sales rose 11% to $746.6M.
• *Tariff Refunds:* Q3 results benefited from approximately $20M in pretax IEEPA tariff refunds, adding $0.40 to diluted EPS.

*Analog Devices ($ADI) beat Q4 revenue and earnings estimates, driven by strong growth across industrial and communications markets, while Q1 earnings guidance came in slightly below expectations.*

• *Q4 Revenue:* $4.37B vs. $4.32B est. (+42% YoY).
• *Adjusted EPS:* $4.06 vs. $3.88 est. (+80% YoY).
• *Margins:* Adjusted gross margin rose 470 bps YoY to 74.5%, while adjusted operating margin expanded 880 bps to 52.3%.
• *Q1 Guidance:* Revenue of $4.4B ± $150M vs. $4.36B est. Adjusted EPS of $3.82 ± $0.20 vs. $3.86 est. Adjusted operating margin of 50.5% ± 100 bps.
• *Segment Growth:* Industrial $2.2B (+55%), Automotive $1B (+21%), Communications $706.8M (+81%) and Consumer $429.4M (+7%).
• *Record FY26:* Revenue reached $15.2B (+38% YoY), with $6.2B in operating cash flow and $5.5B in free cash flow.
• *Shareholder Returns:* Returned $5.4B through dividends and share repurchases in FY26.
• *Beyond AI:* Despite strong AI infrastructure demand driving data center and semiconductor testing growth, more than two-thirds of FY26 growth came from non-AI markets.

*Best Buy ($BBY) beat Q3 revenue and earnings estimates, posting its strongest comparable sales growth in five years and raising its FY27 outlook.*

• *Q3 Revenue:* $10.24B vs. $9.9B est. (+6% YoY).
• *Adjusted EPS:* $1.62 vs. $1.49 est. (+16% YoY).
• *Comparable Sales:* +6.1% overall, with domestic +6.2%, international +4.9% and online +10.8%.
• *Profitability:* Adjusted operating margin reached 4.4%. Domestic gross margin rose to 24.1% from 23.3%, helped by $41M in tariff refunds and growth in Marketplace and Best Buy Ads.
• *FY27 Guidance:* Revenue raised to $43B–$43.3B from $42.3B–$42.8B, vs. $42.68B est. Adjusted EPS raised to $6.90–$7.05 from $6.70–$6.90, vs. $6.81 est.
• *FY27 Outlook:* Comparable sales growth of 3.4%–4%, adjusted operating margin of ~4.5% and CapEx of ~$750M.
• *Q4 Guidance:* Comparable sales growth of 2%–4% and adjusted operating margin of 4.9%–5.1%.
• *Segment Revenue:* Domestic $9.4B (+6.1% YoY) and International $820M (+3.3% YoY).

*Dick's Sporting Goods ($DKS) beat Q3 revenue and earnings estimates and raised its FY26 profit outlook, with improving comparable sales at both Dick's and Foot Locker.*

• *Q3 Revenue:* $5.13B vs. $5.09B est.
• *Adjusted EPS:* $1.94 vs. $1.40 est. (-6% YoY).
• *Comparable Sales:* Dick's +2.6% and Foot Locker +0.5%, with the U.S. Foot Locker banner growing over 4%.
• *FY26 Guidance:* Revenue of $22B–$22.2B vs. $22.12B est. Adjusted EPS raised to $11.45–$12.30 from $11–$12, vs. $11.42 est. GAAP EPS raised to $11.40–$12.25.
• *FY26 Comps Outlook:* Dick's +3.3%–4%; Foot Locker -2% to flat.
• *Segment Revenue:* Dick's $3.3B (+3% YoY) and Foot Locker $1.8B.
• *Store Expansion:* Opened six House of Sport and three Field House locations, bringing totals to 47 and 55, respectively.
• *GameChanger:* The sports technology platform's 2026 revenue is expected to approach $200M.

*Kohl's ($KSS) beat Q3 revenue and earnings estimates and raised its FY26 outlook, with results benefiting from tax refunds, tariff refunds and real estate sales.*

• *Q3 Revenue:* $3.45B vs. $3.39B est. (+1.3% YoY).
• *Adjusted EPS:* $1.76 vs. an estimated $0.01 loss.
• *Comparable Sales:* +1.2%.
• *Gross Margin:* 41.0% (+145 bps YoY).
• *FY26 Guidance:* Raised diluted EPS outlook to $4.30–$4.50, with net sales and comparable sales expected to be flat to +0.5%.
• *Q4 Guidance:* Diluted EPS of $0.95–$1.15 vs. $0.95 est. Net sales and comparable sales expected to be flat to +2%.
• *One-Time Benefits:* Reported diluted EPS of $2.15 included a $137M tax benefit ($1.16/share), $45M in tariff refunds ($0.28/share) and a $61M real estate sale gain ($0.39/share).
• *Turnaround:* Management described the results as an encouraging milestone but acknowledged significant work remains.

*Medtronic ($MDT) missed Q2 revenue estimates but narrowly beat earnings expectations, reaffirming its FY27 outlook as cardiovascular growth remained strong and the company completed its diabetes business separation.*

• *Q2 Revenue:* $9.36B vs. $9.48B est. (+4.5% YoY).
• *Adjusted EPS:* $1.34 vs. $1.33 est. (-1.4% YoY).
• *Organic Revenue Growth:* +6.5%.
• *FY27 Guidance:* Reaffirmed adjusted EPS of $5.94–$6.00 vs. $5.97 est. and organic revenue growth of 7.25%–7.75%.
• *Segment Performance:* Cardiovascular $3.8B (+10.4%), Neuroscience $2.7B (+3.2%) and Medical Surgical $2.2B (+4.4%), all on an organic basis.
• *Diabetes Separation:* Completed the MiniMed split-off via an exchange offer, described as the largest in MedTech history, generating a $2B gain in Q2 GAAP results.
• *Acquisition:* Announced plans to acquire Contego Medical.
• *Clinical & Regulatory:* Completed Sphere-360 U.S. pivotal trial enrollment, secured new reimbursement codes for Altaviva and Symplicity Spyral effective January 2028, and received FDA clearances for LigaSure RAS and Hugo robotic surgery systems.
US PREPARES TO RAISE TARIFFS ON CHINA, EU, 14 COUNTRIES: WSJ

*Lucid ($LCID), Uber ($UBER) and Nuro have begun fully driverless robotaxi testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, ahead of an expected Q1 2027 commercial launch.*

• *Driverless Testing:* Lucid Gravity robotaxis will operate without safety drivers in Palo Alto, Mountain View, Los Altos and Sunnyvale, with additional cities planned for 2027.
• *Launch Timeline:* Driverless employee rides will begin soon, ahead of the expected public launch in Q1 2027.
• *Fleet Expansion:* Lucid has delivered more than 100 vehicles featuring updated hardware, software and passenger-experience features.
• *Regulatory Approval:* Nuro is now one of six companies permitted to conduct driverless testing on California public roads.
• *Uber Commitment:* Uber previously committed to purchasing at least 35,000 Lucid vehicles equipped with Nuro's Level 4 autonomous driving technology, with plans to expand across dozens of global markets.
• *Commercial Model:* The service will use Lucid Gravity and future midsize vehicles, owned and operated by Uber and its fleet partners and available exclusively through Uber's platform.

*The Trump administration is preparing to raise tariffs on China and dozens of other countries over industrial subsidies that it argues create excess production capacity, flood global markets with cheaper goods and undermine U.S. manufacturers, according to people familiar with the plans.*

• *Timeline:* U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer could unveil the investigation's findings as soon as this week, though timing could change.
• *Expected Tariffs:* The EU, Japan and South Korea will likely face overall rates of 15% or lower, while Vietnam and India could face higher rates based on previous trade agreements.
• *China:* Expected to face higher tariffs than many other countries due to the scale of its industrial subsidies.
• *Scope:* Tariffs would likely cover most imports from targeted countries, excluding certain goods such as steel, aluminum and automobiles already subject to separate national security tariffs.
• *Escalation Risk:* The administration could include provisions allowing further tariff increases if industrial overcapacity worsens or countries fail to make policy changes.
• *Tariff Stacking:* The new levies would likely be added to existing 10%–12.5% tariffs imposed on 60 economies over forced-labor trade concerns, which face a court challenge.
• *Final Rates:* Remain unclear, but officials intend to impose rates similar to those introduced in 2025 before the Supreme Court struck down Trump's initial tariffs in February 2026.
• *Political Context:* The announcement comes amid bipartisan scrutiny of the administration's China policy following Nvidia's ($NVDA) alleged AI chip-smuggling controversy.

*Micron ($MU) faces a potential catalyst on December 9, when CHIPS Act-related restrictions expire, allowing the company to resume stock buybacks. However, recent experience at rival memory-chip makers suggests buybacks alone may not sustain a recovery.*

• *Stock Performance:* Micron fell 6.9% to $658.75 in Tuesday's premarket after surging 19% Monday, remaining approximately 44% below its June record high.
• *Buyback Catalyst:* Investors hope renewed share repurchases will help reverse Micron's recent slump.
• *AI Spending Concerns:* Fears of slowing AI data center investment continue to weigh on the stock due to potential weakness in memory-chip demand.
• *SK Hynix:* Its U.S.-traded shares have fallen 20% since announcing a $29B share repurchase and cancellation plan on August 19.
• *Samsung:* Its Korean-listed shares have declined 37% since announcing a nearly $80B shareholder return program on August 21.

*Wall Street’s focus on $NVDA now shifts to congressional scrutiny, customer financing, and whether the AI rally can hold. Yorkville Ives’ Dan Ives raised his target from $225 to $250, while Raymond James reaffirmed $350, the highest target in this roundup.*

*New Ratings and valuations*
• *Raymond James — Simon Leopold:* Kept Strong Buy. Sees little change in AI fundamentals and is watching Huang’s Dec. 1 House interview and Dec. 3 Senate testimony.
• *Rosenblatt — Kevin Cassidy:* Reaffirmed Buy and $300, citing continuity in product planning and customer relationships.
• *Piper Sandler — David O’Connor:* Reaffirmed Overweight and $230, citing more certainty about Nvidia’s direction.
• *DZ Bank — Ingo Wermann:* Kept Buy and a $240 fair value estimate. Expects a near-term benefit from Huang’s return and flags governance concerns.
• *Morningstar — Brian Colello:* Kept its $250 fair value estimate. The report lists four stars and Very High uncertainty. Colello sees Nvidia as more likely to invest in smaller AI cloud providers.

*Rally and spending outlook*
• *Deepwater — Gene Munster:* Sees room for Nvidia to rebound to $182, citing stronger AI fundamentals than he expected in early November.
• *Goldman Sachs trading desk:* Traders buying back shares to close bearish bets could extend the rally. Investors are still weighing whether the rebound can last.
• *TF International — Ming-Chi Kuo:* Flags power, labor and manufacturing constraints. Sees cloud providers’ spending peaking at different points in 2027–28.

*Customer financing*
• *UBS — Timothy Arcuri:* Nvidia’s roughly $390B in supply commitments give it a reason to keep financing customers to support demand for its chips.
• *BofA Securities:* Tighter disclosure and customer-financing practices could limit Nvidia’s flexibility in the near term and make the business more durable over time.
